elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions."

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York will have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising out of or related to this Agreement, except that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, so the exclusive merits forum is preserved.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The governing law remains New York, which is the preferred rather than the fallback jurisdiction; no Delaware, California, or England and Wales selection appears.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is New York County state and federal courts, not Delaware, California, or London courts.

elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element per the checklist; noted only for completeness that New York law is retained verbatim.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: New York substantive law is retained unchanged and a single inserted sentence supplies exclusive merits jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County with only a temporary injunctive relief carve-out, which under the rule boundaries preserves an exclusive merits forum.

Fallback level is not met (and need not be) because the governing law and forum remain New York rather than Delaware, California, or England and Wales/London; position-completeness is achieved at the preferred level.

Minimality holds: the existing governing-law sentence is untouched, no other language is deleted or paraphrased, and the added sentence is a concise insertion filling a genuinely missing forum term. No survival tails, expense language, procedures, or extra requirements were added.

Intent preserved: the jury waiver, limitation-of-actions period, severability and indemnity references to a "court of competent jurisdiction" are left intact, and the temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out avoids contradicting those retained references. No dangling cross-references or undefined terms are created.

Classification as a deviation is supportable: with no forum designated anywhere in the Agreement, the clause failed the forum element of both the preferred and fallback positions on a material term, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.
